title: Retain the landing or learn first flight; choose the hinge
stage_label: Separate instructional session · Week 2, Day 1 · individually authored
status_note: Written athletic prescription independently reviewed. The first-flight teaching proposal is not a current approved card. Actual facility/athlete readiness, live canonical release and precise separate tumbling remain unverified.
brief: Develop a controllable landing and an understandable hinge decision without changing both demands at once. An athlete with a known flight or nonflight task retains it while considering a manageable hinge variant/hold. An athlete ready for first-flight instruction learns a small in-place bilateral takeoff and terminal hold while keeping unloaded hip work. The retained knee/push/pull/brace sets support full-body participation and respect the recent stopping, running and throwing lessons.
quality_target: The athlete performs the exact assigned flight/nonflight action, owns its comfortable finish and resets on cue. Separately, the hinge shows controlled hip-back motion and the athlete can explain why today uses bodyweight, a familiar pair or a first manageable implement lesson. Actual successful flight, extra steps, cue needs, grip/setup, load and response are recorded; planned attempts are not a pass.
continuity: Actual OR-02 landing/hip and more recent OR-03–05 response or direct equivalents → one named new learning demand today, with other anchors retained/reduced → OR-15 consolidates the actual landing and hinge record, then OR-19 verifies the independently eligible branch. Adjacent OR-07 still needs its own controlled stop/announced-exit checks. Use the preserved map together with the active detailed-outline amendments; attendance and age grant no prerequisite.
audience: Ages12–14 are the reference, not beginners. All three age prescriptions and within-age routes are explicit. Five weekdays are offered, not required. A continuing athlete with demonstrated competencies need not repeat this module. D supplies the listed teaching opportunities; L uses no-flight main work and unloaded hip work. Current experience, attention, coordination, growth-related changes, actual recent dose, sport/tumbling load and restrictions determine the choice independently for each role.
readiness: Before delivery review actual OR-02 flight versus grounded status and geometry, recent stopping/running/throwing/support response and the most recent hinge dose. First-flight eligibility can be established from current counted grounded preparation, but that is not successful-flight evidence. Comfortable basic hinge must be established before loading; a prior row or partial squat does not establish two-DB handling. First-flight keeps hip unloaded. A retained known nonflight task can accompany independently eligible DB instruction; jump skill is not a strength gate. If both the primary movement and basic hinge are unfamiliar, keep the smallest counted unloaded hinge instruction and sufficient supervision, or defer that role rather than introduce a second loaded skill.
equipment_space: PLANNING ONLY:15 separate3 × 3 m personal bays in three columns of five, with additional peripheral coach access and clear sightlines. Center the first-flight start so at least1.5 m clear radius is available; actual body, arm, balance/fall space and surface fit must be inspected. This model does not establish that3 m is sufficient for every athlete. Retained forward targets keep the actual0.8 × 0.6 m reference rectangle and0.10/0.20 m centers used previously when independently appropriate; markers are not minimum-distance pass lines. First flight has no forward marker or height quota. No box, obstacle, drop, rebound or partner catch. Two qualified coaches supervise one main athlete at a time. S1 requires two suitable stations, each with an individually fitting stable elevated table/rack for two dumbbells: four active dumbbells total, matched to the two athletes; actual kg and support height recorded. No pickup from the floor or child carrying through active bays is assumed. Later rows require five suitable benches and five manageable single dumbbells; compatible implements may be reused only with the stated transition. Pressing uses five stable individually fitting supports; brace uses five mats. Breathing needs five leg supports; suspension alternative needs five verified anchors. All inventory, geometry and staffing are unverified operating assumptions.
coaching_flow: Athletes remain in their personal bays for preparation and the main landing lesson. P1 uses three groups of five; P2 five waves of three simple already eligible/grounded actions. Main releases one athlete every15 s, with both coaches observing and no other athlete practicing. Coaches use an actual verified viewing/repositioning plan;7 s between8 s bouts is not permission to cross an active landing area. Hip then uses eight paired slots for15 athletes, one coach per active athlete; the final pair has one athlete. Use each child’s declared route, not a common load. The remaining Strength roles use three groups of five with two/three athletes per coach. More teaching/clearance time delays release and removes a later uncompleted opportunity; it never creates more work.
clock: Explosiveness / retained landing or first flight
Strength / hinge decision and familiar support
time_rules: All timings include explanation, setup, actual attempts, reset, handling, equipment movement, water and transitions. Starts are earliest opportunities. Do not force cadence, depth, height or handling to meet the clock. Count faulty/partial actions within the listed dose and record what happened. Delays remove remaining work; no extra test, make-up effort or penalty exercise follows.
preparation_note: Use the complete reviewed instructional base below, preserving recognizable order, no-flight regressions and concluding hinge/squat checks. Its profile name does not require OR-01 attendance. Exactly two targets follow: P1 the unloaded hinge and P2 the route-specific retained/grounded finish, using60 +120 =180 s. First-flight P2 contains no takeoff. Any current assessment action occurs within a listed repetition; no added jump or loaded trial precedes the main work.

exercises.name: Rehearse the owned unloaded hinge
exercises.mapping: HINGE-BW — existing local authored source, teaching dose override
exercises.set_purpose: One short counted set observes hip-back motion before the later hinge decision. It provides the current unloaded-hinge evidence when that action is established today; it is not an uncounted screen or loaded-RDL pass.
exercises.execution: Remain in the assigned bay. Cross arms at the chest, soften knees, move hips back over3s and stand in1s through a comfortable range. Coach demonstrates how a squat differs; athletes perform only the listed hinge repetitions.
exercises.cues: Soft knees; hips back; quiet trunk; stand tall.
exercises.errors: Turning the action into a deep squat, reaching for a stretch, looking up sharply, holding breath or adding repetitions while another group practices.
exercises.rationale: The hinge remains a recurring anchor. Unloaded position rehearsal prepares the eventual bodyweight hold or independently eligible implement lesson without adding grip fatigue before landing practice. No loaded comparison rep is added.
exercises.metadata: Method: counted position rehearsal. Tenets: Strength/Body Control/Coordination. Pattern: bilateral hip hinge. Equipment: marked bay; no implement.

exercises.competency: All ages use the listed small comfortable range. Prior evidence or the actual first listed P1/base action must establish controlled unloaded hinging before the loaded branch is considered. Unknown or unsuitable hinge control stays on the small unloaded teaching route or is deferred. This gate is independent of jump status.
exercises.progression: Retain actual arms-crossed position, range and cadence. If a recent smaller dose exists, use the single-repetition P1 hold rather than forcing two; all ages then perform one 4 s rep plus 2 s setup. No load or extra screen is added.
exercises.continuity: Actual OR-02/03/04/05 or direct equivalent hip record → one counted unloaded rehearsal → S1 retains actual compatible unloaded work or teaches a separately eligible two-DB variant. First-flight instruction never accompanies a hinge load increase.

exercises.name: Rehearse the selected grounded or established finish
exercises.mapping: Retained JUMP-STICK or SNAP-STICK; first-flight preparation uses the separately labeled SQUAT-BW slow-position teaching task
exercises.set_purpose: One counted action rehearses the actual retained finish. On the first-flight branch it establishes grounded descent/hold/rise and stop-cue participation only; the first takeoff occurs in E1. No hidden jump test is added.
exercises.execution: Use the same verified personal bay. Retained forward routes use the actual qualified bilateral stance, relaxed-arm start and small forward swing into the 0.10 m rehearsal marker, then 2 s hold and same-bay reset. Grounded snap uses a comfortable tall reach, controlled rapid descent with arm drive down, continuously grounded feet and a 2 s hold. First-flight preparation and the slow-position route use 3 s comfortable partial squat, arms comfortably forward for balance, 2 s hold, 1 s rise and 2 s reset; no flight.
exercises.cues: Comfortable position; two feet; hold the finish; stand and reset on instruction.
exercises.errors: Treating a held squat as successful flight, silently changing a retained target, taking off in the grounded route, bouncing, forcing depth or adding a correction repetition.
exercises.rationale: Target choice follows the main task. A newcomer needs current grounded control before the first taught takeoff; an already eligible jumper rehearses the retained forward finish. A rapid snap and a slow squat retain different readiness and movement identities.
exercises.metadata: Method: one observed rehearsal. Tenets: Body Control / Balance / Strength; coordination integrated. Pattern: retained jump/land or a separately logged grounded descent. One bilateral flight landing would be one event and two foot contacts.

exercises.competency: Retained forward routes require actual independent low bilateral jump/landing and exact target/control evidence, not attendance. Rapid snap requires its own grounded descent and reach. First-flight teaching may use actual comfortable slow descent, stable two-foot hold, controlled rise and conduct observed during this counted P2 or direct prior evidence. That permits instruction of a first takeoff, not a flight-competency pass. Failed/uncertain P2 control keeps the independently eligible grounded route or defers the affected task.
exercises.progression: Hold the actual target, surface, arm rule and hold. No first-flight attempt occurs in preparation. All ages follow the same domain gates; older age does not introduce flight or a farther marker.
exercises.continuity: Actual OR-02 landing/nonflight record or current counted grounded instruction → this one precise rehearsal → E1 retains the known task or teaches first bilateral flight. OR-15/19 later retain the actual resulting branch; P2 never grants throwing or main JUMP permission.

exercises.name: Retain the known landing or learn a first small takeoff
exercises.mapping: JUMP-STICK for retained forward routes; FIRST-FLIGHT-TEACH for new in-place instruction; SNAP-STICK / SQUAT-BW for distinct nonflight routes
exercises.set_purpose: Every listed single-attempt set practices one controlled finish under individual observation. Retained routes preserve OR-02’s useful opportunities: 3 standard / 2 compressed. First-flight D uses only 2 standard / 1 compressed introductory opportunities; the first is the counted instruction and the second standard opportunity repeats the same task after recovery only if appropriate. Neither route pursues height, distance, fatigue or a valid-rep quota.
exercises.execution: Retained forward route: the same qualified 0.20 m main target or 0.10 m short target, relaxed arms beside the trunk with a small natural swing, bilateral takeoff/landing, 2 s terminal hold and ordinary same-bay reset. First flight: begin in place, feet comfortably apart, arms beside the trunk. Use one shallow continuous down-and-up countermovement and small natural arm swing to make a gentle bilateral vertical takeoff; land on both feet near the start, absorb through a comfortable bend, hold 2 s, then stand/reset. There is no paused squat-jump start, deliberate rapid snap-down, overhead target, rebound or minimum jump height. If the feet do not leave the ground, record an attempted instruction with no successful flight credit. Grounded routes use the exact P2 action and remain continuously grounded.
exercises.cues: First flight: small jump straight up; land on both feet and hold. Retained forward: small known jump; own the same finish. Grounded: down, hold, stand. Everyone: wait for your release and reset fully.
exercises.errors: Calling grounded work a jump, awarding a forward-jump pass from an in-place attempt, a second bounce, forced height, uncontrolled extra step, knee/trunk collapse, an inappropriate arm action or added screening attempts.
exercises.rationale: First-flight acquisition closes a real prerequisite gap in the on-ramp rather than requiring a prior jump to teach jumping. The existing squat-jump/countermovement profiles still contain prior-flight gates, so their names/approvals are not borrowed. Athletes with a known landing retain its geometry while learning a hinge decision. A known nonflight task can also be retained alongside independently eligible strength instruction; jump ability is not a prerequisite for strength.
exercises.metadata: Method: blocked individual single-attempt instruction with full recovery. Tenets: Explosiveness / Balance / Body Control; coordination and resilience through controlled landing. Source/output gains are not claimed. Equipment: inspected personal bay and flat markers only.

exercises.competency: First-flight entry requires actual grounded control, comfortable bilateral rise/descent and intended small arm-swing range, conduct, an inspected clear landing area and qualified direct supervision. Use actual prior or counted preparation observations; do not add a screening swing or jump. Prior successful flight is not required. One or two initial attempts do not automatically establish repeatability or main entry. All ages use the same small first-flight dose; current readiness, not age, selects it. L contains no flight. Retained forward routes retain their stricter actual prior/direct equivalent jump gates. exercises.continuity: Actual OR-02 low jump/grounded control and OR-03–05 response → retained known finish OR separately taught first in-place takeoff today → OR-15 consolidates the actual recorded task, and OR-19 verifies only an actually eligible branch. exercises.name: Choose and explain a manageable hinge task
exercises.mapping: HINGE-BW arms-crossed unloaded anchor; DB-RDL two-dumbbell standard-tempo variant, with explicit first-implement teaching context
exercises.set_purpose: One hip set has the named job selected before release: retain actual unloaded control; teach a small unloaded set when history is unknown; retain a familiar two-DB variation; or learn the new two-implement setup and controlled hinge at a manageable load. A first DB set changes grip/arm position, handling and resistance as one newly taught variant, not merely a numerical weight increase. Prior two sets are deliberately reduced to one; recent one-set/low-repetition work stays small.
exercises.execution: Unloaded: arms crossed at chest, soft knees, send hips back for 3 s and stand for 1 s through the actual owned range. Loaded: two dumbbells, one in each hand, palms facing inward and arms long without forcing elbow lock; begin tall with loads close to the thighs. Maintain soft knees and an organized trunk/pelvis, hinge back for 3 s through the owned hamstring-limited range, stand for 1 s, then park both loads safely. Do not turn this into a floor-touch or squat-depth target. The two loads begin on individually fitting stable elevated supports immediately at the station, not on the floor or in another active bay.
exercises.cues: Hips back; soft knees; keep both loads close; stand tall; stop with control left; park both loads.
exercises.errors: Assuming bodyweight/row competence proves two-implement handling, forcing a lower range, load drifting away, grip/balance loss, breath holding, adding a test set, or increasing weight because the child is older.
exercises.rationale: Hip leads with an eight-minute standard or six-minute compressed block so the load/hold decision is explained and observed. Two athletes work at a time, one per coach, rather than five simultaneous first-time pickups. Each athlete receives one set. The first-flight branch keeps unloaded work; a retained known flight or nonflight task can accompany independently eligible DB instruction without an irrelevant jump prerequisite. The remaining four roles stay familiar and small.

Unknown basic hinge uses the 1 × 2 unloaded teaching route for every age and booking, or is deferred; no extra unloaded screen is inserted in S1. First loaded success need not preexist: the scheduled pickup/top-stand observation establishes grip and support fit before the first loaded rep. If pickup/grip/control is unsuitable, the coach manages safe set-down and the counted set ends; no replacement loaded or unloaded set is added. Current restrictions are not overridden by a lighter prescription.
exercises.progression: Choose the route from actual variation and response, then choose repetitions from the actual recent compatible dose. D does not automatically raise a prior 2/3/3-rep low dose to 3/4/4. A first-flight attempt cannot accompany a loaded hinge route. A load increase is never required; familiar DB routes hold their actual pair, and first-DB instruction uses a manageable verified light pair without mid-set increases. Record a lower completed dose/stop when necessary. The next relevant hinge decision uses this actual response.

timing_narrative:
**Two preparation targets,180 s.** P1 uses60 s:15 s instruction in the existing bays, then groups of five start15/30/45 s. D uses2 hinges ×4 s +2 s setup =10 s; L or a smaller actual preparation hold uses1 ×4 s +2 s =6 s. Last D group ends55 s, leaving5 s. P1 is a single short rehearsal with no repeated set; inter-set rest is not applicable. The earliest same-athlete gap to the distinct P2 task is50 s after default D or54 s after the smaller hold, including complete setup/reset. P2 uses120 s:15 s demonstration/reminder, then five three-athlete waves at15/30/45/60/75 s. One8 s action per athlete, final wave ends83 s. Remaining37 s is route/readiness recording and preparation for the main lesson, not more reps. No bay-to-lane travel is hidden.

**Main standard.**15–20 min is technique/route explanation and coach demonstration with no extra athlete trial. Retained forward or grounded routes have opportunities at20/26/32 min; first-flight D uses only20/26. Main individual offsets are0,15,…210 s; one8 s action/hold/reset each, with7 s for verified coach sightline/repositioning before the next athlete. A round finishes218 s after its start. Same-athlete recovery across6 min rounds is352 s after the complete envelope, above60 s. Latest retained-route finish35:38; first-flight finish29:38. Remaining time includes feedback on actual attempts, demonstration of the hinge decision, water and Strength setup by45 min. Do not fill earlier finishes with jumps.

**Main compressed.**10–15 min instruction and route/readiness decision; retained routes use15/22 min rounds, first-flight D only15 min. Same individual offsets/envelopes; retained-route repeat recovery412 s. Last retained action25:38; first flight18:38. Feedback, hinge demonstration, water and transfer fit before35 min. L uses its actual grounded action at the retained3 standard /2 compressed opportunities; it contains zero flight. A preselected one- or two-attempt cap simply removes later opportunities and preserves the same complete action/rest.

**Priority hip instruction.** Standard45–53 gives480 s:60 s demonstration/setup, eight paired slots start60/105/150/195/240/285/330/375 s,45 s each, then60 s final feedback/transition from420–480. Compressed35–41 gives360 s:60 s demonstration/setup, paired slots60/95/130/165/200/235/270/305 s,35 s each, then20 s transition from340–360. Pair index is athlete index divided by2 and rounded down; the final slot contains athlete14 only. Each active athlete has one coach and one set. The first-DB handling envelope is20 s total:7 s pickup from the declared elevated support,3 s standing grip/top-position observation before the first loaded rep,6 s controlled set-down and4 s clear/reset after the last rep. Standard first-DB work is3 reps for9–11 or4 for12–14/15–18 ×4 s +20 s =32/36 s; compressed first-DB work is2 reps for every age ×4 s +20 s =28 s. The shorter compressed dose preserves time to teach both implements. Familiar-DB handling is10 s (4 pickup,4 set-down,2 reset), giving at most26 s with4 reps. Unloaded handling is5 s, at most21 s with4 reps. Actual slower teaching/handling consumes spare time and can remove a later unfinished set; never add a substitute trial. A first pickup that cannot be controlled ends before any loaded hinge.

Brace69–75:360 s,60 s setup and groups60/140/220 s. Compressed41–44 knee and44–47 push: each180 s,45 s setup and groups45/85/125 s. Pull47–51:240 s,60 s setup and groups60/120/180 s. Maximum bouts: squat25 s, push17 s, both-side row52 s, heel taps26 s; breathing replacement40 s plus15 s quiet recovery. The compact row ends232 s within240; compact breathing recovery ends210 s. Each is the proposed small in-place single shallow countermovement with modest natural arm swing,2 s bilateral landing hold,8 s complete envelope, bodyweight/easy2–3/10, at least60 s rest. No height/distance quota, added screening takeoff, rebound or external load. P2 for every age/booking is1 ×1 slow grounded3 s lower/2 s hold/1 s rise/2 s reset, bodyweight/easy2/10,60 s rest. This observes grounded readiness only. Both L bookings use an independently eligible grounded main route instead; first-flight L has zero assigned jumps. First-flight athletes use only unloaded S1 routes. Unknown/unsuitable basic hinge does not become a loaded task: use the small counted unloaded instruction or defer it.

**Retained landing choices, every age.** Qualified forward reference: P2 one0.10 m rehearsal, E1 standard D3 ×1 or compressed D2 ×1 at the actual eligible0.20 m target. Qualified short route keeps both P2/E1 at0.10 m, with the same dose. Both use relaxed-arm start/small natural swing, bilateral flight/landing,2 s hold and8 s complete envelope, easy3/10 bodyweight and60 s rest. Keep the actual previously used target rather than convert a short result to the reference. Both flight routes are unavailable in L. Each action needs its own comfortable entry; if no action fits, defer the domain. Grounded work does not supply flight or throwing credit.

**Fewer main opportunities, all ages.** When actual recent dose/readiness calls for retention below the reference, choose one total E1 opportunity in either booking, or two total where that route’s reference contains at least two. Begin at the first listed round and omit later rounds. Variant, per-attempt dose, effort and rest remain exactly as above. A first-flight compressed session remains one even under a two-opportunity ceiling. These are explicit count caps, not extra options added together. Any faulty attempt consumes its opportunity; a switch to a grounded action uses a remaining opportunity without replacement.

**Unloaded S1 choices, explicit by age.** Reference-compatible D:9–11 one×3;12–14 one×4;15–18 one×4 in either booking. Smaller actual-dose hold, in D or L:9–11 one×2;12–14 one×3;15–18 one×3. Unknown hinge history:9–11 one×2;12–14 one×2;15–18 one×2 in either booking/mode, explicitly taught rather than described as retained. Every route uses arms-crossed bodyweight hinge,3 s back/1 s stand,5 s setup/exit, at least5 good reps in reserve and60 s recovery. Preserve an actually smaller recent record through the matching hold or a further recorded reduction; no age/date-based increase. First-flight uses only these unloaded choices. The current small instruction does not invent a prior record.

Two actual familiar individually fitting loads,3 s lower/1 s stand, at least5RIR,10 s known pickup/set-down/reset and90 s recovery. Retain the actual pair and owned range; do not interpret a listed reference as permission to increase a more recent lighter dose. Record kg per dumbbell and total. These routes require actual grip/setup competence and a retained known primary task; they never accompany new first-flight instruction. L uses unloaded S1.

**First two-DB S1 teaching, D only.** Standard:9–11 one×3;12–14 one×4;15–18 one×4. Compressed:9–11 one×2;12–14 one×2;15–18 one×2. Use a coach-selected actually manageable light pair from verified stock, not a universal age load. Basic unloaded hinge must already be observed in counted preparation or prior evidence. The first scheduled elevated pickup/top-standing setup observes actual grip and handling; first loaded hinge is the first listed repetition, not an extra test.3 s lower/1 s stand, at least5RIR by coach judgment,20 s handling as itemized,90 s recovery. If grip/setup is unsuitable, stop and manage safe set-down; no extra unloaded or lighter loaded set is added. For a smaller actual recent hinge dose, first-DB count holds are explicit: a one-repetition ceiling gives all ages one rep in either D booking; a two-repetition ceiling gives all ages two reps in either D booking; a three-repetition ceiling gives all ages three reps standard D and two reps compressed D. Each ceiling keeps the full20 s first-setup handling,3 s lower/1 s stand,at least5RIR,90 s recovery and all first-DB gates. Select no more than the actual recent compatible count. These sets therefore take24/28/32 s for1/2/3 reps. A capped first-DB set never borrows the familiar10 s handling or prior-DB-competence gate. This newly taught variant holds the actual known flight/nonflight primary task. No simultaneous new flight or larger landing/output demand. L stays unloaded.

**Brace replacement:** all ages/modes1 ×4 comfortable breaths, nominal2 s in/3 s out without holds or forced depth,20 s total setup/exit and15 s quiet recovery. Calves/heels supported on a verified suitable surface, bilateral comfortable reach, no heel pull or hip lift. It replaces S5 and grants no heel-tap moving-limb pass;5 leg supports needed.

**Already qualified suspension pull replaces S4:** all ages D1 ×4 bilateral reps; L1 ×3,2 s lower/1 s pull,5 s handling,60 s recovery and at least5RIR. Use verified secure anchors and approximately70° body angle to floor, actual angle recorded. This is its own grip/support/body-line task, not automatically authorized by an unsuitable bench. It replaces one row set; no safe anchor/eligibility means unavailable.
workload_narrative:
The instructional base retains its separately counted no-flight actions. P1 adds2 unloaded hinges in D or1 in L/its small hold; P2 adds one explicit retained jump or grounded action. Retained flight has4 total planned flight opportunities standard D or3 compressed D before any cap: one P2 plus3/2 E1. First-flight has zero preparation flight and2/1 planned main opportunities, not2/1 guaranteed successful jumps. Grounded routes have zero assigned flight. Count an actual successful bilateral landing as one event/two foot contacts; failed takeoff, extra steps, partial or faulty landings and their actual contacts are logged as observed, not erased. No sprint, throw, rebound, maximal jump or physical finisher is added.

Five planned Strength sets, one per role. Hip may be unloaded, familiar two-DB or first-implement instruction, with distinct setup/handling and exact age/repetition counts above. A recent one-set or smaller repetition history is held; an older compatible two-set history is deliberately reduced. A bodyweight-to-two-DB change introduces a new implement variant, not an invisible load increase. First-flight keeps unloaded hip work. Knee/push D3/4/4 and L2/3/3; squat5 s per rep +5 s setup, push3 s +5 s setup. Row D4 each/L2 each at4 s per rep +10 s side change +10 s handling. Heel taps D2 each/L1 each at4 s +10 s setup; alternatives replace the sole set. Actual kg, range, supports, attempts, assistance/cues and response remain unknown until recorded.

Recent OR-03 braking/stance, OR-04 running and OR-05 throwing/handling/push-pull still matter even if OR-06’s nominal counts are small. Hinge implements and later rowing both use grip; supported pressing and brace work add their own demands. No combined fatigue score or universal contact ceiling is invented. More recovery or deferral may be appropriate; flexible attendance creates no missing-work debt.

age_scaling_policy.equal_dose_reason: Short low-effort preparation is not age-based overload. Explicit equal doses across ages are deliberate; task skill, body size, comfortable range and current readiness decide the variant.
age_scaling_policy.readiness_independent_of_age: Experienced younger athletes may use qualified familiar actions; unfamiliar older athletes use instruction. Age never grants flight, rapid descent, floor support, loaded patterns or cue response.

layout_and_timing_assumptions.layout: Three columns of five distinct 3 m × 3 m personal bays: 15 independent working spaces. Five athletes share a lane assignment, never an overlapping crawl corridor.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.additional_space: Unobstructed peripheral coach circulation/access/egress and separately verified start, runoff and return corridors are additional to the 9 m × 15 m bay rectangle. The marked rectangle is not the total facility footprint.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.travel: Standing paths remain in personal bays. Short forward passes are at most 1.6 m; backward/lateral spans 1 m or less except 1.5 m carioca. Individually check full hand-walk/plank footprint before use.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.orientation: All bays face one end. Complete a pass and stop before ordinary walking return within that same bay. No crossing between athletes or concurrent opposite-direction traffic inside a bay.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.coaches: Familiar shared practice: one coach scans A/B and one scans B/C with clear oblique views. Three-wave teaching/checks: both coaches watch one active lane and split five athletes 2/3; other lanes stand. Clear views of all active feet/trunks are required.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.wave_handover: The active lane finishes standing, then the next lane starts on cue. The 2-second change (3 seconds for floor teaching) is a cue change, not relocation. Athletes stay in their own bays.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.equipment: Flat markers, bottles outside active rectangles, clean dry nonslip surface. No partner support, unstable props or unverified anchor is assumed.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.setup_before_clock: Mark/inspect space before class. Readiness/restriction information must be available. First demonstration includes stop cue and immediate comfort check. Unknown restrictions or inability to follow safe directions require individual resolution, never assumed clearance.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.clock_definition: Row time = demonstration + waves × individual execution envelope + explicit wave handovers + reset/transition. The individual envelope includes stated steps, pauses and returns. Shared practice means separate bays, not 15 times one athlete dose.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.tempo_rule: Execution envelopes are estimates for the stated variant, not speed commands. If safe learning/movement needs longer, use contingency, remove optional work or revise the booking. Never rush to validate arithmetic.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.bay_to_target_transition: Base ends at 12:00 full or 7:00 compact with athletes standing in bays. Reserve exactly 180 seconds for exactly two parent-owned target tasks. The parent exemplar defines the split and charges bay-to-start gathering, demonstrations, observed holds, rehearsal, exit and return within those 180 seconds. Use the parent-defined allocation; do not double-charge gathering or hide it before the base ends.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.physical_validation_status: UNVERIFIED: measured space, body fit, sightlines, surface, shared-floor schedule and target corridors have not been observed. Arithmetic does not certify physical feasibility.

teaching_and_competency_policy.full_familiar: Sixteen ordered slots with reminder demonstrations only. SP-11/SP-12 explicitly repeat mastered A-March because exact B/C identities are unverified.
teaching_and_competency_policy.compact_familiar: Eleven slots in original relative order. Omit SP-04, SP-10, SP-11, SP-12, SP-14. Retain floor purpose through the declared stationary-bear modification; hinge and squat remain last.
teaching_and_competency_policy.or01_full: Eleven recognizable slots in 12 minutes. Easy march replaces jog; optional crossing/flight/B/C complexity is omitted; lunges lose rotation/depth; floor flow becomes knees-down rock-backs; descent is slow; basic march/foot-roll precede observed hinge and partial squat-to-stand. After the easy raise, all actions are demonstrated and observed in three five-athlete waves.
teaching_and_competency_policy.or01_compact: Same eleven recognizable slots in 7 minutes. Basic walking/stepping/foot-roll can follow the coach in separate bays. Lunge, floor, slow drop, hinge and partial squat remain serialized in three observed five-athlete waves. One hinge and one squat cycle are readiness observations; qualification belongs to subsequent instructional work.
deferred_complexity: Traveling bear crawl and new complete plank/downward-dog flow
Full toe/ankle contact and overhead squat-to-stand range when unavailable
teaching_and_competency_policy.what_deferred_means: Practice the simpler named component in its original place; log performed variant and unfilled demand. Teach additional complexity in a relevant later instructional module. Do not silently pass it, substitute a generic unrelated warm-up or add teaching outside the clock.
teaching_and_competency_policy.partial_competency: Existing evidence can support a familiar variation, independently of age. Preparation completion does not unlock a main family: no-flight lowering is not landing, marching is not running, rock-back is not tumbling, and no throw/cue gate is tested here.
teaching_and_competency_policy.correction_limit: Use visible contingency for actual slower movement or brief corrective repeat and record time/dose/contacts. If essential teaching remains incomplete, mark profile/session REVISE and use the 12-minute instructional base or a justified booking adjustment. Never consume the reserved target time or speed up movement.
teaching_and_competency_policy.optional_reduction_order: For familiar full, remove SP-12 then SP-11, then SP-04/SP-10/SP-14 as readiness/purpose permits. Record omissions and revised clock. Compact/OR already omit these; beyond contingency, further necessary omissions require explicit review rather than an unqualified complete-base claim.

flight_not_qualified_overlay.application: For otherwise familiar athletes whose flight is unqualified, independent of age. This can accompany an independently qualified throw-only main branch, but does not itself authorize throwing or a cue.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-01: Easy march in place for the same 60 seconds full or 50 seconds compact; no flight.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-08: Retain a separately qualified no-flight rapid descent. If unlearned, slow drop squat to stick: 3 × 8-second envelopes, each 2 s lower + 2 s hold + 1 s stand + 3 s reset; no travel. Record changed variant.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-10: Omit four A-Skip hop landings; freed time is recovery, not another drill.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-13: Eight alternating no-flight foot-roll actions, four each side: 8 × 2 s + 4 s standing reset = 20 seconds; no travel. Log changed variant.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-14: Omit six bilateral pogo landing events; no substitute jump.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.accounting: Subtract omitted flight events and record actual time/contacts. Reduced-impact preparation grants no JUMP-T, REACT-T, throwing, early-release or go/no-go qualification.

records.name: Backpedal
records.purpose: Rehearse controlled backward travel and orientation.

card_mapping_status.limit: A related backpedal-to-sprint identity is not this slow preparation task.

records.setup: Face the same end of the room. Mark 1 m behind the start; two short backward steps reach it, then two forward walking steps return. No turn or crossing.
cues: Short steps under you; look forward.
Check the clear space behind you before moving.
common_errors: Long reaching steps and backward lean.
stop_rules: Stop for obstacle, balance loss or pain; use ordinary walking return only when clear.

competency_rule.observe: Controls both backward steps and forward return with balance and stop-cue response.
competency_rule.pass_scope: Preparation observation only. A completed repetition does not grant a main-family, loaded-strength, flight, throwing, cue-response or tumbling qualification.
competency_rule.record: Log selected profile, actual variant/dose, comfort, response to cue, omissions and not-observed actions. No actual results are invented.

records.name: Lateral shuffle
records.purpose: Access lateral movement with organized feet and controlled orientation.

card_mapping_status.limit: This low-intent short shuffle is not reactive cutting.

records.setup: Start centered. Step-close without crossing for 1 m right and 1 m left back to start. Repeat only for the familiar dose.
cues: Stay facing forward; step then close.
Own the stop.
common_errors: Reaching past the bay or racing the return.
stop_rules: Stop if feet collide, boundary control fails or discomfort appears.

competency_rule.observe: Maintains forward orientation and controlled step-close both directions.

competency_rule.record: Log selected profile, actual variant/dose, comfort, response to cue, omissions and not-observed actions. No actual results are invented.

records.name: Inchworm → plank → bear crawl → downward dog (ordered slot)
records.purpose: Prepare shoulder/wrist support, trunk control, hip movement and floor transitions with low fatigue.

verified_local_names: Inchworm → plank → bear crawl → downward dog
Inchworm to World’s Greatest Stretch (related legacy flow)
card_mapping_status.limit: Exact composite not established. Stationary limb unloads explicitly replace traveling bear crawl for 15-bay delivery. Knees-down rock-backs are a declared partial-purpose regression, not an exact approved composite. The proposed stationary substitution is specifically four separately mastered single-limb lifts with full replants, not an unspecified weight shift or contralateral crawl.

records.setup: One athlete per dry nonslip 3 m × 3 m bay. Entire floor footprint fits before use. No shared slow-crawl lane or following crawler. Coach checks hand/knee comfort before support. Familiar bear support uses one limb at a time: left hand, right hand, left foot, right foot. A lift means the whole selected hand or foot briefly clears the floor by about 1–2 cm; it is not merely a weight shift. Fully replant and settle before the next limb.
cues: Hands comfortable; breathe with controlled trunk.
Quiet unhurried transitions; soft knees in downward dog.
Keep the trunk quiet; lift one contact only, then fully replant before the next.
Do not lift opposite hand and foot together.
common_errors: Forced straight knees or shoulder range.
Starting the next lift before the previous contact is fully replanted.
Rotating or sagging the trunk to clear the limb.
stop_rules: Stop for wrist/shoulder pain, slipping, trunk-control loss or inadequate footprint.
Use contingency or record incomplete rather than rushing floor entry.

Omit the familiar bear-lift component if any single-limb lift/replant has not already been mastered; use the entire named instructional floor profile and its coaching clock, or record incomplete purpose. No new bear-lift teaching is assumed inside the familiar reminder.

competency_rule.observe: Comfortable actual support and floor entry/exit. Rock-back does not pass plank/bear or tumbling support. For familiar bear lifts, each selected contact clears briefly, fully replants, and the trunk remains quiet before the next lift.
competency_rule.pass_scope: Preparation observation only. A completed repetition does not grant a main-family, loaded-strength, flight, throwing, cue-response or tumbling qualification.
competency_rule.record: Log selected profile, actual variant/dose, comfort, response to cue, omissions and not-observed actions. No actual results are invented.

full.variant: Inchworm → high plank → stationary bear-position single-limb lifts/full replants → downward dog → standing

execution_segments.name: Move to hands-and-knees then low bear position
Left hand, right hand, left foot, right foot: one contact clears 1–2 cm then fully replants before the next
execution_segments.execution_detail: Per 2-second lift/replant: about 0.5 s clear the selected contact, 0.5 s fully replant, 1 s settle with all four contacts before the next lift; quiet trunk throughout.

full.tempo: Known controlled flow. Four single-limb lift/replant cycles at 2 s each: brief 0.5 s lift, 0.5 s full replant, 1 s stable reset. Do not start the next lift before stable full contact.
full.effort: Easy and conversational; no maximal speed, height, stretch or fatigue target.

records.name: Squat-to-stand with overhead reach — concluding check
records.purpose: Observe knee/hip/trunk organization through a comfortable sequence.

card_mapping_status.limit: Source 62 is review state. Familiar prescription follows candidate variant sequential-bilateral-reach-squat-to-stand: standing hinge/contact, comfortable squat, one controlled overhead reach per assigned side, stand/reset. Assigned order is left then right. Current exact dose/profile eligibility remains unverified. The OR thigh-supported partial version remains an explicitly different modification pending variant review.

records.setup: Same three five-athlete observation waves. Comfortable stance/reachable contact points; no forced toe touch or depth. Coaches see feet and trunk. Familiar source-linked sequence assigns LEFT reach and return, then RIGHT reach and return while the opposite hand maintains its comfortable toe/ankle contact; stand only after both reaches. Each reach stays in controlled comfortable range.
cues: Use comfortable range and a stable foot.
Reach without forced rib flare; stand smoothly.
Left reach and return, right reach and return, then stand; do not skip a side.
common_errors: Counting one reach as completion of the familiar sequential-bilateral cycle.
stop_rules: Stop for pain or uncontrolled balance/trunk; use declared partial sequence if comfortable. Longer teaching uses contingency or records incomplete.

competency_rule.observe: Observe actual sequence, foot pressure and control; not a loaded squat or tumbling qualification.
competency_rule.pass_scope: Preparation observation only. A completed repetition does not grant a main-family, loaded-strength, flight, throwing, cue-response or tumbling qualification.
competency_rule.record: Log selected profile, actual variant/dose, comfort, response to cue, omissions and not-observed actions. No actual results are invented.

workload_and_tumbling_interface.purpose: Finish warm and organized, not tired. Effort about 2/10 and conversational; this is not overload or conditioning.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.full_flight: Four unilateral A-Skip hop landings and six bilateral pogo landing events are explicitly prescribed in the familiar full profile. Timed easy jog and ankling also carry impact; their actual flight/contact detail is recorded instead of fabricated.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.compact_flight: A-Skip/pogo are omitted, but easy jog still has impact and ankling actual contacts remain in the record. Compressed is not automatically impact-free.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.or01_flight: No intentional flight in the first-visit profiles; no landing gate is thereby passed.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.upper_body: Familiar floor work includes a 4-second high plank, brief bear-position support/unloads and downward-dog access. Count wrist/shoulder/trunk demand alongside throwing, pressing, bracing and separate tumbling. Rock-back support is still support.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.tumbling: The separate 30-minute tumbling/Body Control allocation remains unprescribed here. Share actual comfort, support/impact exposure and observations with its coach. Its later load and staffing remain unverified.

reviewable_modifications.alternative_arithmetic: At 32 seconds per athlete, five serial waves in three parallel lanes require at least 160 seconds of work before demo/clearance, versus 32 seconds with separate bays: 128 seconds extra. Adding that to the complete full clock exceeds 720 seconds without another explicit change.

counting_conventions.primary_repetitions: Always interpret reps_total with count_unit and count_definition. Mixed flow constituents, side counts, foot contacts and timed segments are not interchangeable.
counting_conventions.segment_repetitions: Each execution segment has its own count_unit. Its duration remains repetitions × seconds_each. Primary count contributions convert the segment counts to the record primary unit; complete cycles remain the accepted unit.
counting_conventions.SP-09_and_fallback_normalization: A-March primary counts are now individual steps: 8 familiar (4 each side) or 4 OR (2 each side). Bilateral cycle counts are explicit secondary metadata; actual movement/time unchanged.
counting_conventions.SP-13_correction: Familiar full/compact is 16 individual ankling task contacts, eight each foot; OR01 full/compact is four individual foot-roll/replace actions, two each foot. No execution duration or physical dose changed.
counting_conventions.contact_rule: Landing events and per-foot landing contacts are separate. Timed jogging/actual ankling flight count stays null when not predetermined, never zero by default.
